text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran the replay harness on last week's prod traces after the anonymization patch (PR #1423). Seeing ~7% tail P95 latency regression on raptor-small. Need parity investigation.

ajay: Can you paste the exact run id + command? Did you keep kernel selection flags and quant profile identical to the golden runs?

maria: Run id `run-20260310-01`. Command I used:
```
./replay --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-10/part-01.gz \n  --anon-policy=pr1423 \n  --sample-seed=42 \n  --model=raptor-small \n  --kernels=auto \n  --kv-cache=enabled \n  --out=run-20260310-01
```

sam: I pulled profiling for run-20260310-01. Short summary: CPU spent more time in tokenization/normalization, but the main perf delta is more GPU kernel launches and smaller effective batch sizes because anonymized prefixes vary more. Top lines from profiler: 
```
[PROFILE] avg_batch_size=3.2 (was 4.8)
[PROFILE] kernel_launches_per_req=12 (was 8)
[PROFILE] kv_cache_hit_rate=0.82 (was 0.87)
[PROFILE] p95_latency=134ms (was 125ms)
```

leah: Anonymization changed prompt lengths distribution — sampling might be biased. We should check determinism: replay with `--preserve-order --seed` and run parity checker across token-level outputs. Also validate that kernel selection flags are identical.

ci-bot: parity-check job started for run-20260310-01 (job id: 4583).

ajay: If kernel selector behaved differently, is it because avg_seq crossed a threshold? We recently changed selector thresholds for cuBLAS vs custom kernels.

maria: Here's the parity-check command I ran:
```
python tools/parity_check.py --gold run-20260228 --cand run-20260310-01 --tolerance=1e-3 --mode=token
```

ci-bot: parity-check complete for job 4583: mismatches=12/1000. Most mismatches are truncated system prompts or differing anonymized markers. Full diff: /tmp/parity-20260310-01.log

ajay: If mismatches are truncation/anonymization tokens only we can normalize before compare. We should add `--mask-anon` option to parity checker.

maria: I'll re-run with a normalization step that collapses anonymized ids to `<id>`. Also plan to run an apples-to-apples synthetic experiment that preserves prompt length distribution but removes KV cache to measure worst-case.
```
./replay --trace s3://prod-traces/... \n  --anon-normalize=collapse-ids \n  --synthetic=length-preserving \n  --kv-cache=disabled \n  --out=run-20260310-02
```

ops-qa: Agree. Also run with fixed batching (e.g. `--batch-size=4`) vs `auto` so we can isolate batching heuristics. I'll spin up loadgen to run both configs for 10k requests each.

sam: Quick note from profiler: kernel selector picked cuBLAS path for matmul when avg_seq > 512. The anonymizer increased avg_seq slightly on many traces so more requests hit cuBLAS, hence more kernel launches and slightly higher overhead per request. :thinking_face:

leah: @maria can you attach the anonymization diff or PR link? Need to audit tokenization changes.

maria: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay/commit/abc123 — the anonymizer replaces long ids with UUID stubs which turned out to add 2–3 tokens in many system prompts.

ajay: Potential quick fixes: 1) normalize UUID stub to a single token; 2) add a parity-mode that masks anonymized tokens before comparison. Both should be quick. :thumbsup:

maria: On it. Will run `run-20260310-03` with normalization + parity-mode and post results later today. /cc @leah @ajay @sam

ci-bot: enqueue job 4587: replay run-20260310-03 (queued on eng-runtime-loadgen).

maria: Thanks all — next steps: run normalization + parity-mode, run synthetic apples-to-apples with fixed batching and kv-cache toggles, then compare profiler traces (avg_batch_size, kernel_launches, kv_cache_hit_rate, p95). Will update with numbers.

ops-qa: I'll collect the synthetic run artifacts and put them in GCS under `gs://redwood-perf/anon-audit/2026-03-10/`.

sam: If anyone wants quick wins: add a guard in kernel selector telemetry to log threshold-crossing reasons so we can correlate with anonymized-length changes.

leah: Sounds good. Keep the parity diffs minimal — aim for < 5 mismatches per 10k after normalization.

maria: Will do.
